title: Marked homotopies induce parameterized precomposition on relative flat mapping objects
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, degreewise products and internal functor simplicial sets of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and marked simplicial sets, marking-preserving maps, coordinatewise product markings and $K^\flat,K^\sharp$ of [lem-coef-marked-point-cartesian-model]. Fix a small simplicial set $S$ and marked simplicial sets $U,V,W$ with maps to $S$, in a fixed containing universe. Define $\operatorname{Map}^\epsilon_S(P,Q)_k$ to be the marked maps $P\times(\Delta^k)^\epsilon\to Q$ over $S$, with base map ignoring the parameter, for $\epsilon=\flat,\sharp$; operators restrict the parameter.

Let $h_0,h_1:U\to V$ be marked maps over $S$, and let $H:U\times(\Delta^1)^\flat\to V$ be a marked map over $S$ with these endpoints. The formula which sends a $k$-simplex $(a,\tau)$, where $a:V\times(\Delta^k)^\flat\to W$ is marked over $S$ and $\tau:\Delta^k\to\Delta^1$, to
$$U\times\Delta^k\longrightarrow W,\qquad (u,v)\longmapsto a(H(u,\tau(v)),v)$$
defines a simplicial map
$$\Phi_H:\operatorname{Map}^\flat_S(V,W)\times\Delta^1\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}^\flat_S(U,W).$$
Its endpoint maps are the simplicial precomposition maps $h_0^*,h_1^*$. Its component at a vertex $a:V\to W$ is the edge represented by $a\circ H$. If $H$ also preserves the additional markings of $U\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp$, each such component belongs to $\operatorname{Map}^\sharp_S(U,W)_1$. No fibrancy of $U,V,W,S$ is assumed, and the simplices $a$ need not have invertible parameter edges.

proof.text: First the displayed mapping sets have the specified simplicial operators. For $\alpha:[m]\to[k]$, restriction sends $a:P\times(\Delta^k)^\epsilon\to Q$ to $a\circ(\mathrm{id}_P\times\Delta(\alpha))$. A simplicial map carries a degenerate edge to a degenerate edge; thus $\Delta(\alpha)$ preserves the flat markings, and it preserves the sharp markings because every target edge is marked. Coordinatewise product markings make this restriction marked, and its base map still ignores the parameter. Restriction along identities and composites is respectively identity and iterated restriction, by equality of the composites. This verifies the simplicial-set structure for both values of $\epsilon$.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, marked internal Hom setup immediately before Remark 3.1.3.1; agent-written coordinate verification: restriction operators

proof.text: Fix $k$, $a$ and $\tau$ as in the statement. Define $b_{a,\tau}$ degree by degree: for $u\in U_r$ and $v\in(\Delta^k)_r$, put $b_{a,\tau,r}(u,v)=a_r(H_r(u,\tau_r(v)),v)$. For any $\beta:[t]\to[r]$, naturality of $a,H,\tau$ gives $$W(\beta)b_{a,\tau,r}(u,v)=a_t(H_t(U(\beta)u,\tau_t(\Delta^k(\beta)v)),\Delta^k(\beta)v)=b_{a,\tau,t}(U(\beta)u,\Delta^k(\beta)v).$$ Products and operators are degreewise by [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], so this is precisely the condition that $b_{a,\tau}:U\times\Delta^k\to W$ is a simplicial map.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, marked internal Hom setup immediately before Remark 3.1.3.1; agent-written coordinate verification: simpliciality in the source degree

proof.text: A marked edge of $U\times(\Delta^k)^\flat$ is a pair $(e,d)$ with $e$ marked in $U$ and $d$ degenerate. Since $\tau$ is simplicial, $\tau(d)$ is degenerate. Consequently $(e,\tau(d))$ is marked in $U\times(\Delta^1)^\flat$, so $H(e,\tau(d))$ is marked in $V$. The pair $(H(e,\tau(d)),d)$ is then marked in $V\times(\Delta^k)^\flat$, and $a$ takes it to a marked edge of $W$. Thus $b_{a,\tau}$ is marked. Write $q_U,q_V,q_W$ for the given base maps. In every degree, $$q_W b_{a,\tau}(u,v)=q_V H(u,\tau(v))=q_U(u).$$ Hence $b_{a,\tau}$ lies in $\operatorname{Map}^{\flat}_S(U,W)_k$.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, marked internal Hom setup immediately before Remark 3.1.3.1; agent-written coordinate verification: flat marking and relative base condition

proof.text: For a parameter operator $\alpha:[m]\to[k]$, put $a_\alpha=a\circ(\mathrm{id}_V\times\Delta(\alpha))$ and $\tau_\alpha=\tau\circ\Delta(\alpha)$. For every degree and every pair $(u,w)$ in $U\times\Delta^m$, $$b_{a_\alpha,\tau_\alpha}(u,w)=a(H(u,\tau(\Delta(\alpha)w)),\Delta(\alpha)w)=b_{a,\tau}(u,\Delta(\alpha)w).$$ The right side is the restriction of $b_{a,\tau}$, and the left side is the formula applied to the restriction of $(a,\tau)$. Since all simplicial operators are restrictions, the maps $(a,\tau)\mapsto b_{a,\tau}$ commute with all of them. Together with Steps 2-3 this constructs the asserted simplicial map $\Phi_H$.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, marked internal Hom setup immediately before Remark 3.1.3.1; agent-written coordinate verification: simpliciality in the parameter degree

proof.text: At endpoint $i\in\{0,1\}$ the $k$-simplex of $\Delta^1$ is the constant map with value $i$. The formula becomes $b_{a,i}(u,v)=a(h_i(u),v)$, which is the stated precomposition map $h_i^*$ in each degree. At a fixed vertex $a:V\to W$ of the mapping object, its degenerate $1$-simplex is $a\circ\operatorname{pr}_V:V\times\Delta^1\to W$, because mapping operators restrict the parameter. Evaluating $\Phi_H$ at this simplex and $\mathrm{id}_{\Delta^1}$ gives $(u,t)\mapsto a(H(u,t))$. Thus the edge obtained by restricting $\Phi_H$ to $\{a\}\times\Delta^1$ is represented by $a\circ H$.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, marked internal Hom setup immediately before Remark 3.1.3.1; agent-written coordinate verification: endpoints and vertex components

proof.text: Assume now that $H$ also preserves the markings of $U\times(\Delta^1)^\sharp$. A marked edge there is any pair $(e,d)$ with $e$ marked in $U$ and $d$ any edge of $\Delta^1$. By the extra hypothesis $H(e,d)$ is marked in $V$, and the marked vertex map $a:V\to W$ carries it to a marked edge of $W$. Therefore $a\circ H$ is marked with sharp parameter. It is over $S$ by the same base equality as Step 3, so it represents an element of $\operatorname{Map}^{\sharp}_S(U,W)_1$. Every construction and verification used only the given maps and marking definitions; no fibrancy or invertibility condition on the parameter edges of $a$ enters.

source.place: Section 3.1.3, marked internal Hom setup immediately before Remark 3.1.3.1; agent-written coordinate verification: sharp component condition

lean.statement: theorem marked_homotopy_precomposition {S : SSet.{u}} (U V W : Over S) (h₀ h₁ : U ⟶ V) (H : (productLeft U).obj (flat (Δ[1] : SSet.{u})) ⟶ V) (endpoints : ∀ (i : Fin 2) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (x : U.left.underlying.obj n), H.left.val.app n (x, stdSimplex.const 1 i n) = (if i = 0 then h₀ else h₁).left.val.app n x) : ∃ Φ : mapFlat V W ⊗ (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}) ⟶ mapFlat U W, (∀ (n m : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (a : (mapFlat V W).obj n) (τ : (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}).obj n) (x : U.left.underlying.obj m) (v : (stdSimplex.obj n.unop).obj m), (Φ.app n (a, τ)).left.val.app m (x, v) = a.left.val.app m (H.left.val.app m (x, (yonedaEquiv.symm τ).app m v), v)) ∧ (∀ (i : Fin 2) (n : SimplexCategoryᵒᵖ) (a : (mapFlat V W).obj n), Φ.app n (a, stdSimplex.const 1 i n) = productMapLeft (if i = 0 then h₀ else h₁) (flat (stdSimplex.obj n.unop)) ≫ a) ∧ (∀ a : V ⟶ W, (Φ.app _ ((mapFlat V W).σ 0 (mapFlatVertex a), yonedaEquiv (𝟙 (Δ[1] : SSet.{u})))).left.val = H.left.val ≫ a.left.val) ∧ ((∀ (e : U.left.underlying _⦋1⦌), e ∈ U.left.marking → ∀ d : (Δ[1] : SSet.{u}) _⦋1⦌, H.left.val.app _ (e, d) ∈ V.left.marking) → ∀ a : V ⟶ W, ∃ b : (mapSharp U W) _⦋1⦌, b.left.val = (Φ.app _ ((mapFlat V W).σ 0 (mapFlatVertex a), yonedaEquiv (𝟙 (Δ[1] : SSet.{u})))).left.val)
